statements.text: Back pain began 08/04/2026 after lifting a laundry basket, 8 weeks before this visit.
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/21/2026: acute osteoporotic T12 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.
Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture.

Radiology Report
Date: 09/21/2026
Patient: Debby Berge, 67-year-old female

Examination: MRI thoracolumbar spine

Findings:
MRI thoracolumbar spine 09/21/2026: acute osteoporotic T12 compression fracture with bone marrow edema on STIR imaging.

No other acute abnormalities are noted in the thoracic or lumbar spine.

Impression:
Acute osteoporotic compression fracture at T12 with associated bone marrow edema, consistent with recent injury.

Recommendations:
Clinical correlation is advised. Follow-up imaging may be considered based on clinical course.

Spine Intervention Consultation
Date: 09/28/2026
Patient: Debby Berge, 67-year-old female

History of Present Illness:
Back pain began 08/04/2026 after lifting a laundry basket, 8 weeks before this visit. Pain NRS 5/10 despite 7 weeks of optimal non-surgical management with oxycodone 5 mg as needed, a thoracolumbar brace and activity modification. Pain has worsened over the past two weeks despite bracing.

Clinical Findings:
Seen in the outpatient spine clinic; not hospitalized for this fracture. Back pain is primarily from lumbar spinal stenosis rather than the fracture.

Plan:
Referred for DEXA bone density testing and osteoporosis education; enrolled in the osteoporosis treatment program. Continue current pain management and bracing. Monitor symptoms and consider further intervention if pain persists or worsens.
